title: Insulin Pump Program Terms: Enrollment and the Tier a Program Bills
content:
**1. Opening a program.** An Insulin Pump Program is opened when Larkfield accepts a referral for this product line, and the tier written on the program is fixed by the coverage the program bills, never by the customer's preference.

**2. Locating the tier.** The tier is located from the coverage record named on the program: the coverage record's plan type and coverage order must equal the tier's entry gate, and the self-pay tier is used only when no coverage record is named.

**3. Coverage in effect.** The coverage record named on the program must be in effect on the date of the write: its effective date is on or before that date and its termination date is empty or on or after that date. Both boundary days count as in effect: a record whose effective date or termination date is the date of the write satisfies the test.

**4. Original Medicare beneficiaries.** A customer with an in-effect Original Medicare Part B coverage record cannot be enrolled on the self-pay tier for an item Medicare covers, because Larkfield submits a claim for every Medicare-covered item it supplies to a Medicare beneficiary; that customer is enrolled on the Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program, and an item or quantity Medicare will not pay is handled under the program's advance-notice-of-liability rules.

**5. Two coverages.** When a customer has two in-effect coverage records, the one whose coverage order is primary fixes the tier and the secondary coverage only receives crossover or secondary claims; a coverage record whose coverage order is secondary never fixes the tier.

**6. Clinical qualification.** Any clinical qualification in the tier's entry gate is read from the program's own clinical fields as documented on the prescriber's written order and medical records, never from the customer's description alone.

**7. Program changes.** A program change rewrites the coverage reference and the tier together when the customer's insurance changes, and rewrites prescriber or product fields when a newer written order changes them; a change never rewrites status, and after a tier change the next refill may draw only on an authorization grant recorded under the new tier.

**8. Coverage not on file.** A coverage the customer reports that is not on file cannot be written onto a program, because coverage records are created only by Larkfield's benefits verification team after the payer confirms eligibility.

## Schedule of entry gates

| Tier | Coverage record | Further entry conditions | Clinical qualification documented |
|---|---|---|---|
| Insulin Pump Self-Pay Program | none named | written order required | insulin-requiring diabetes |
| Insulin Pump Commercial HMO Program | commercial HMO, primary | network referral required | insulin-requiring diabetes; multiple daily injections for 6 months; diabetes education completed |
| Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program | commercial PPO, primary | — | insulin-requiring diabetes; multiple daily injections for 3 months; diabetes education completed |
| Insulin Pump Medicare Advantage Program | Medicare Advantage, primary | — | C-peptide or autoantibody result; multiple daily injections for 6 months; glucose testing 4 times a day or CGM use; diabetes education completed |
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program | Medicare Part B, primary | — | C-peptide or autoantibody result; multiple daily injections for 6 months; glucose testing 4 times a day or CGM use; diabetes education completed |
| Insulin Pump Medicaid Program | Medicaid, primary | — | insulin-requiring diabetes; multiple daily injections for 6 months; diabetes education completed |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A customer whose only in-effect coverage record is a commercial PPO plan with coverage order primary is placed on the Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program, whatever tier the customer asks for.
- A customer holding a primary Medicaid record and a secondary commercial HMO record is placed on the Insulin Pump Medicaid Program; the HMO record receives only secondary claims.
- A coverage record with a termination date one day before the date of the write is not in effect on that date; one terminating on the date of the write is.
